steps.player: Can you teach me the basics of Woodcutting and Firemaking, please?

steps.text: Of course... look for this icon on your minimap to find areas of trees.
If the player is not carrying an axe:
If the player's inventory is full:

steps.npc: I'd give you an axe to chop trees with but you don't have room in your inventory.
As you're already here, have an axe so that you can chop the trees around me.

steps.text: bronze axe

steps.npc: When you see a likely looking tree, appreciate its beauty, then simply click on it to chop it down.
When you have a full inventory of logs, you have a choice. You can take it to the bank, there's one on the roof of the castle in Lumbridge, or you can burn them.

steps.text: To find a bank, look for this symbol on your minimap after climbing the stairs of the Lumbridge Castle to the top. There are banks all over the world with this symbol.
If the player is not carrying a tinderbox:

steps.npc: Ah, you've lost your tinderbox have you? Have another!
Click on your tinderbox, then click on one of the logs in your inventory, this will attempt to light a fire that you can use for cooking.

options.text: What is that cape you're wearing?
I already know a bit about Woodcutting and Firemaking, any tips?
options.condition: If the player has level 20-28 Woodcutting

steps.text: If the player is not carrying an axe:
If the player's inventory is full:

steps.npc: I'd give you an axe to chop trees with but you don't have room in your inventory.
As you're already here, have an axe so that you can chop the trees around me.

steps.text: bronze axe

steps.npc: Choose carefully where and what you chop, you can get different trees in different places throughout the land.
Make sure you hang on to your logs, don't throw them away as you can get valuable firemaking experience from them! Look out for other things too...
Watch out for the tree spirits, they really don't like you chopping trees, they can really do some damage if you're not paying attention...
Don't forget you can always use logs for fletching experience too.
Yes, you'll need lots of logs if you want to be a good fletcher. Talk to the ranging tutor for more information.

steps.npc: As you get better and better you'll find that you can chop trees such as Maple and Yew! These are very good for firemaking.
Of course, they're also very useful for fletching.
Also, look out for birds' nests, you never know what our feathered friends have been collecting. Jewellery and Clue scrolls maybe?

options.text: Tell me about different trees and axes.
options.condition: If the player has level 19-98 Woodcutting

steps.player: Tell me about different trees and axes.

steps.text: Almost every tree can be chopped down. Normal logs will be produced by chopping 'Trees' and Oak logs will come from chopping 'Oak Trees'. You can find Oak trees in amongst normal trees scattered about the lands.
Willow trees will yield willow logs. You'll find willows like to grow near water, you can find some south of Draynor.
Maple logs can be gleaned from Maple trees. You'll usually find Maple trees standing alone amongst other trees.
Yew trees are few and far between. We do our best to cultivate them. Look for the tree icon on your minimap to find rare trees. Try North of Port Sarim.

options.condition: If the player has level 29-98 Woodcutting

steps.text: Magic trees are... magic. A difficult wood to work with, but worth it for the rewards. Find them in the areas south of Seers village or on the East side of the Mage Arena.

steps.npc: Hollow trees can be found in the Haunted Woods east of Canifis, but be careful of the leeches.

steps.text: Bronze axes are easy to get, simply go visit Bob in his shop in Lumbridge, or talk to me if you have mislaid yours.

steps.npc: As you progress in your combat skill you will find you can wield your woodcutting axe as a weapon, it's not very effective, but it frees up a slot for another log.

steps.text: As your woodcutting skill increases you will find yourself able to use better axes to chop trees faster.... anything up to steel you can buy from Bob's axe shop.
Rune axes can be player made with very high level smithing and mining. They can also be obtained through killing one of the fearsome tree spirits, though this is very rare.

options.text: What is that cape you're wearing?

99-woodcutting.npc: Wow! It's not often I meet somebody as accomplished as you in Woodcutting! Perhaps you should become the tutor, instead of me! Seeing as you're so skilled, maybe you are interested in buying a Skillcape of

steps.npc: Ok, come back to me if you change your mind.

steps.text: If on F2P world:

steps.npc: I can't sell you one here. Try talking to me later.

steps.text: If on a members world:

steps.npc: Anybody who has spent as much time cutting trees as you deserves the right to own one. Wearing this cape will increase your chance of finding bird's nests. That'll be 99000 coins, please.
Well go chop down a few mahogany trees and sell the timber; then you'll be able to afford one.

steps.text: If the player does not have 99000 coins:

steps.player: But, unfortunately, I don't have enough money with me.

steps.npc: Well come back and see me when you do.

steps.text: If the player has 99000 coins:

steps.npc: Excellent! Wear that cape with pride my friend.

steps.text: If the player has 99000 coins but no inventory space:

steps.npc: Unfortunately all Skillcapes are only available with a free hood, it's part of a skill promotion deal; buy one get one free, you know. So you'll need to free up some inventory space before I can sell you one.

steps.text: If on a members world and the player already owns a Woodcutting cape:

BpbZ4K.player: What is that cape you're wearing?

BpbZ4K.npc: This is a Skillcape of Woodcutting, wearing one increases your chance of finding bird's nests. Only a person who has achieved the highest possible level in a skill can wear one.
